Package io.micronaut.dev.http

@NullMarked package io.micronaut.dev.http
What development mode adds to an HTTP server: requests wait for a reload in progress, and a failed compilation is shown instead of the stale application.
Since:
5.3.0
Author:
graemerocher
  • Related Packages
    Package
    Description
    io.micronaut.dev
    The development mode launcher: MicronautDevMain starts an application behind a reloadable class loader and the DevRuntime recompiles, restarts and reports as sources and resources change.
  • Classes
    Class
    Description
    DevGateFilter
    Holds requests while a reload is in progress, up to DevManifest.requestHoldTimeout() and then answers them with a 503 and a Retry-After; answers them with the diagnostics while the last compilation failed: a page for a browser, a structured 503 for anything else.
    DevRouter
    The router of a context in development mode: it forwards to the application's router, the one the context would inject without it (DefaultRouter unless the application replaced it), and swaps that router for a new one when the routes change within a generation.
    DevRouter.NoPrimaryApplicationRouter
    Holds unless the application declares a primary router of its own, which this router would compete with for every injection of a Router: the routes then reload by restarting only.
    DevServerSockets
    The listening sockets of the application's HTTP servers, bound once and kept for the life of the development runtime, so that the port stays bound across generations: a connection that arrives while one generation stops and the next starts waits in the socket's backlog, and the next generation's server accepts it, instead of being refused.
    LiveReloadScriptFilter
    Adds the LiveReload client script to HTML pages, and a no-store cache header so that a refresh always reaches the server.
